title: Birbal and the Carpenter
summary: A hasty carpenter ruins expensive sandalwood timber for the royal throne. Birbal teaches the court a masterclass in precision and foresight.
full_text:
A master carpenter named Kalu was commissioned to build an imperial throne using rare, fragrant red sandalwood brought from the forests of Mysore at immense expense.

Eager to finish quickly and claim his gold reward, the carpenter sawed, planed, and hammered in frantic haste. When he assembled the four legs of the throne, he was horrified to discover that one leg was two inches shorter than the others, causing the throne to wobble absurdly!

Panicking, Kalu hastily sawed two inches off the second leg. Now the third leg was too long! He sawed the third leg, and then the fourth, until the majestic imperial throne was reduced to a low, comical stool!

Akbar was furious: 'You fool! You have ruined ten thousand rupees worth of rare sandalwood through your careless haste! Guards, throw him into prison!'

Birbal stepped forward: 'Sire, spare the carpenter. His folly is a living demonstration of an ancient rule of craft.'

Birbal asked the carpenter: 'Kalu, what measuring tool did you use before sawing the wood?'

Kalu wept: 'None, my lord! I merely estimated with my eye and cut in haste!'

Birbal turned to Emperor Akbar and the assembled ministers:

'Sire, Kalu's mistake is the universal error of humanity. The carpenter's proverb warns: "Measure twice, cut once." In his rush to finish, he cut without measuring, and then cut again to hide his first mistake, ruining the whole timber.

'How often do kings and ministers do the very same thing in governance? In hasty anger, a ruler passes an ill-considered decree. When the decree causes trouble, instead of pausing to measure the truth, he passes a second hasty law, and a third, until the noble throne of justice is whittled down to dust!

'Whether carving sandalwood or passing imperial laws, patience, foresight, and precise measurement before action are the only safeguards against ruin.'

Akbar took the lesson to heart. He pardoned the humbled carpenter, ordered him to rebuild the throne under Birbal's supervision, and adopted the motto: 'Deliberate with patience; act with precision.'

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Birbal and the Carpenter"?
options: Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
